answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted identity: an agent must lock a meaningful bond before it can transact, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a glacier carving a valley — steady, verifiable work over time — rather than arriving instantly. A newcomer may wander freely and observe, but only sustained, attested contributions move it toward the zenith of trust where high-value deals unlock. Sybils stay cheap to spawn yet worthless to use, because trust is earned, not claimed.
